task_description: CLI permissions snapshot integration testing - Record IAM roles assumed and actions performed during integration tests as snapshots

features.description: Create core permissions tracking module with AWS SDK v3 middleware
steps: Create new package directory `tools/@aws-cdk/permissions-snapshot/` with standard structure (package.json, tsconfig.json, jest.config.js, eslint.config.mjs)
Create `lib/sdk-middleware.ts` implementing AWS SDK v3 middleware plugin that intercepts all API calls before sending
Implement middleware to extract and record: service name (e.g., 's3'), action name (e.g., 'PutObject'), request parameters (sanitized)
Add special handling for STS service to track AssumeRole, AssumeRoleWithSAML, AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity calls and record assumed role ARNs
Create `lib/permissions-tracker.ts` with PermissionsTracker class providing: start(), stop(), getRecordedPermissions(), clear() methods
Implement thread-safe collection of permissions data using a singleton pattern to work across multiple SDK client instances
Create `lib/types.ts` defining TypeScript interfaces: RecordedAction, RecordedRole, PermissionsSnapshot
Create `lib/index.ts` with clean public API exports
Add unit tests in `test/sdk-middleware.test.ts` using aws-sdk-client-mock to verify middleware correctly intercepts calls
Add unit tests in `test/permissions-tracker.test.ts` to verify tracker accumulates and deduplicates permissions
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware successfully intercepts AWS SDK v3 API calls without affecting their execution
All API calls are recorded with service name, action name in a normalized format
STS AssumeRole calls specifically capture the role ARN being assumed
PermissionsTracker can be started/stopped and provides deduplicated results
Unit tests pass with >80% code coverage
Package builds successfully with `yarn build`

features.description: Implement permissions snapshot file management and comparison
steps: Create `lib/snapshot-format.ts` defining the JSON schema for permissions snapshot files
Implement snapshot format with sections: metadata (timestamp, test name), assumedRoles (sorted array of role ARNs), actions (sorted array of {service, action} objects)
Create `lib/snapshot-writer.ts` with function to write PermissionsSnapshot to a `.permissions.snapshot.json` file
Create `lib/snapshot-reader.ts` with function to read existing snapshot file or return null if not exists
Create `lib/snapshot-comparator.ts` implementing deep comparison of two snapshots, returning detailed diff
Implement diff output showing: added roles, removed roles, added actions, removed actions
Add `lib/snapshot-utils.ts` with helper functions: normalizeSnapshot (sort and deduplicate), formatDiff (human-readable output)
Add unit tests in `test/snapshot-writer.test.ts` verifying correct file output format
Add unit tests in `test/snapshot-reader.test.ts` verifying reading and parsing of snapshot files
Add unit tests in `test/snapshot-comparator.test.ts` verifying accurate diff detection
acceptance_criteria: Snapshot files are written in deterministic order (sorted) for consistent git diffs
Snapshot comparison correctly identifies additions and removals
Missing snapshot file is handled gracefully (treated as empty for comparison)
Snapshot format is human-readable JSON with proper indentation
All snapshot operations are idempotent (same input produces same output)

features.description: Integrate permissions tracking with integration test execution flow
steps: Add `@aws-cdk/permissions-snapshot` as dependency to `tools/@aws-cdk/integration-test-deployment/package.json`
Modify `lib/integration-test-runner.ts` to import and initialize PermissionsTracker before test execution
Add middleware registration to intercept SDK calls made during `cdk bootstrap` and `cdk deploy` operations
Implement snapshot file path resolution: place `.permissions.snapshot.json` alongside existing `.snapshot` directory
Add logic after test execution to compare recorded permissions against existing snapshot
Implement test failure when permissions snapshot differs and `--update-snapshots` flag is not set
Add `--update-permissions-snapshot` CLI flag to update permissions snapshots on intentional changes
Add `--skip-permissions-snapshot` CLI flag to disable permissions tracking for specific test runs
Modify test output to clearly indicate when permissions snapshot comparison fails with actionable diff
Update `bin/index.ts` to parse and pass through the new CLI flags
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests record permissions during execution without affecting test behavior
Permissions snapshots are created in predictable location alongside template snapshots
Tests fail with clear error message when permissions change unexpectedly
The `--update-permissions-snapshot` flag successfully updates snapshot files
The `--skip-permissions-snapshot` flag bypasses all permissions tracking
Existing integration test functionality remains unchanged when permissions tracking is disabled

features.description: Add documentation and configuration options for permissions snapshot feature
steps: Create `tools/@aws-cdk/permissions-snapshot/README.md` explaining the feature purpose, usage, and snapshot format
Document how to interpret permissions snapshot diffs and common scenarios requiring updates
Add configuration file support `permissions-snapshot.config.json` for customization options
Implement ignore patterns to exclude specific services or actions from tracking (e.g., CloudWatch Logs for debugging)
Add section to main repository CONTRIBUTING.md explaining permissions snapshot workflow for contributors
Document the aggregated snapshot analysis use case - how to extract all permissions needed for a CDK command
Create example showing typical CI/CD integration and how to handle snapshot updates in PRs
Add inline JSDoc comments to all public APIs in the permissions-snapshot package
acceptance_criteria: README clearly explains what permissions snapshots are and why they exist
Configuration options are documented with examples
Contributors understand how to update permissions snapshots when making legitimate changes
Documentation explains how to use aggregated snapshots to derive minimum IAM permissions
All public APIs have JSDoc comments that appear in IDE intellisense
